word_order: SOV | verbs and predicates appear at the end of clauses/sentences in the sample (e.g. 「報じました」「必要があります」「行われました」).
punctuation_present: sometimes — sentence-final and clause punctuation (。、) and brackets/quotes appear in many but not every short unit.
register: formal written news/encyclopedic prose (newswire and informational sentences).
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer to wait for predicate (verb/adjective) to appear before finalizing a segment because Japanese is head-final. Treat full-width sentence punctuation (。、) and closing brackets/quotes (」, ）) as attached to the preceding segment. Avoid splitting on slashes, interpuncts, parentheses or inside Latin/parenthetical citations (e.g. "(James et al., 1995)") or numeric groupings. If a segment ends with contrastive/continuation tokens like が／けど／しかし, keep them with the following text rather than closing the segment.
